Quick reference

Course glossary

#N/A

The requested value is not available or not found.

#REF!

A reference is invalid, often after deletion.

#SPILL!

An error indicating the result cannot occupy its required cells.

AND

Returns TRUE only when all arguments are TRUE.

AVERAGE

Returns the arithmetic mean of numeric values.

AVERAGEIF

Averages values meeting one condition.

AVERAGEIFS

Averages values meeting multiple conditions.

Absolute reference

A reference with fixed row and column.

Add-in

An optional component that extends Excel features.

Analysis ToolPak

Excel’s statistical analysis add-in.

Analytical workflow

A repeatable sequence from question to evidence and communication.

Annotation

Text or markers explaining important chart events.

Append

Combining tables by stacking rows.

Applied Step

One transformation recorded in sequence.

Approximate match

A lookup that chooses a nearest band rather than an exact key.

Argument

An input supplied to a function.

Assumption

A condition required for a method’s interpretation.

Auditability

The ability to trace an output back to its source and transformation.

AutoFill

A feature that copies formulas or extends patterns.

AutoFilter

The dropdown filtering interface on a range or table.

Axis

A scale that maps values to chart position.

Boolean multiplication

A method for combining AND conditions in array formulas.

CLEAN

Removes many nonprinting characters.

CONCAT

Joins text from arguments or ranges.

COUNT

Counts numeric values.

COUNTA

Counts non-empty values.

COUNTBLANK

Counts blank cells in a range.

COUNTIF

Counts cells meeting one condition.

COUNTIFS

Counts records meeting multiple conditions.

CSV

A plain-text comma-separated values file.

Calculated column

A table column where one formula is automatically filled down.

Calculation chain

The dependency order used to recalculate formulas.

Cell address

A column letter and row number identifying a cell.

Color scale

A gradient mapping values to colors.

Comparison

An expression that returns TRUE or FALSE.

Composite key

An identifier formed from more than one field.

Concatenation

Combining text values into one string.

Conditional format

A style applied when a rule is true.

Conditional mean

An average calculated for a defined subset.

Constant

A manually entered value rather than a formula result.

Control check

A formula or rule designed to expose an invalid state.

Control total

A trusted count or sum used for reconciliation.

Correlation

A standardized measure of linear association.

Covariance

A measure of joint variation in original units.

Criteria range

The cells tested against a criterion.

Criterion

The condition used to include a row.

Current region

A block of data bounded by blank rows and columns.

Custom list

A user-defined order such as High, Medium, Low.

DAX

The formula language used in the Data Model.

Dashboard brief

The audience, decisions, metrics, and layout requirements for a dashboard.

Data Model

Excel’s relational analytical model containing multiple tables.

Data Table

A what-if tool that recalculates an output across input values.

Data dictionary

Definitions, types, and rules for dataset fields.

Data type

The underlying kind of value stored in a cell.

Date serial

The whole-number representation of a date.

Delimiter

The character separating fields, such as comma or tab.

Denominator

The total used as the base of a rate or proportion.

Dependent

A cell whose formula refers to another cell.

Dimension table

A table describing entities used to group or filter facts.

Distinct list

A collection with duplicate values removed.

Dropdown list

A validation interface for choosing an approved category.

Duplicate key

A key appearing more than once in a supposedly unique table.

Duration

Elapsed time between two date or time values.

Dynamic array

A formula result containing multiple values.

EOMONTH

Returns the last day of a month offset.

Editable input

A deliberately unlocked and documented user-entry cell.

Effective denominator

The number of values actually included in an average.

Encoding

The character representation used by a text file.

Error alert

The response shown when invalid data is entered.

Error value

A special result indicating a formula problem.

Exact match

A match requiring equal key values.

Exact-match zero

The MATCH argument 0 requiring an exact match.

Excel Table

A structured range with built-in data-management behavior.

FILTER

Returns rows or columns meeting a condition.

Fact table

A table of events or measurements at a defined grain.

Fill copy

Replicating a formula into adjacent cells.

Fill handle

The small control used to drag a fill operation.

Filter

A condition that controls which rows are visible.

Filter context

The filters determining which rows contribute to a measure.

Filter state

The active selections affecting displayed results.

Final expression

The calculation returned by LET.

Find

A search for matching values, formulas, or formatting.

Flash Fill

A feature that infers a text transformation from examples.

Formula bar

The area used to view or edit a cell value or formula.

Formula rule

A conditional-format rule driven by a formula.

Freeze Panes

A view feature that keeps selected headers visible while scrolling.

Go To

A command for navigating to a cell, range, name, or special cell type.

Go To Special

A selector for cells with particular properties.

Goal Seek

Changes one input until a formula reaches a target.

Grain

What one row represents in a dataset.

Group By

Aggregating rows by one or more fields.

Grouping

Combining dates or numbers into larger categories.

Handover

Documentation enabling another person to refresh and review the work.

Helper column

A worksheet column used to expose an intermediate calculation.

Holiday range

Dates excluded from workday calculations.

IF

Returns one value for TRUE and another for FALSE.

IFERROR

Returns an alternative result when an expression errors.

INDEX

Returns a value at a position in a range.

Identifier

A code used to distinguish records, usually treated as text.

If-empty argument

The value returned when no records match.

Include array

The TRUE/FALSE array controlling which records are returned.

Input message

Guidance displayed when a validated cell is selected.

Insight

A contextual explanation of an important pattern.

Join kind

The rule determining which matched or unmatched rows remain.

KPI

A metric selected to monitor a defined objective.

Key uniqueness

The rule that each key appears once where a single result is expected.

LEFT

Returns characters from the beginning of text.

LEN

Returns the number of characters in text.

LET

Assigns names to intermediate values inside a formula.

Legend

A key explaining series colors or symbols.

Locale

Regional settings that affect date and number interpretation.

Logical test

An expression returning TRUE or FALSE.

Lookup array

The one-dimensional range searched by XLOOKUP.

Lookup value

The value being searched for.

M language

The functional language underlying Power Query steps.

MATCH

Returns the relative position of a lookup value.

MAX

Returns the largest numeric value.

MID

Returns characters from a specified position.

MIN

Returns the smallest numeric value.

Maintainability

How safely another person can understand and update the workbook.

Measure

A calculation evaluated in the current filter context.

Median

The middle ordered value.

Merge

Combining tables by matching keys and adding columns.

Metric definition

A precise rule specifying how a KPI is calculated.

Mixed reference

A reference with either row or column fixed.

NETWORKDAYS

Counts working days between dates.

Name Box

The box that shows the active cell address and can navigate to a range.

Name Manager

The tool used to create, inspect, and repair defined names.

Name-value pair

A local name and the expression assigned to it.

Named range

A meaningful name assigned to a cell or range.

Null

The absence of a value in Power Query.

Number format

A display rule that does not normally change the underlying number.

OR

Returns TRUE when at least one argument is TRUE.

Operator

A symbol such as +, -, *, /, ^, or > used in an expression.

Outlier

An observation unusually far from the main pattern.

Output sheet

A sheet designed to communicate analysis or results.

Paste Special

Options for pasting values, formulas, formats, or other components.

PivotTable

An interactive summary of a tabular dataset.

Portfolio artifact

A project package demonstrating process, technical skill, and communication.

Power Pivot

Excel data-modeling technology for relationships and calculations.

Power Query

A data connection and transformation engine.

Precedence

The order in which parts of a formula are evaluated.

Precedent

A cell referenced by another formula.

Precision

The number of digits retained in a value.

Project brief

A document defining the question, audience, scope, and deliverable.

Quartile

A boundary dividing ordered data into four parts.

Query

A defined set of connection and transformation steps.

RIGHT

Returns characters from the end of text.

ROUND

Rounds to the nearest specified digit.

ROUNDDOWN

Rounds toward zero.

ROUNDUP

Rounds away from zero.

Range

One or more selected cells.

Raw file

The unmodified source received for analysis.

Recommendation

A proposed action linked to evidence and constraints.

Reconciliation

Comparing independent totals or records to confirm agreement.

Refresh

Updating a PivotTable from its current source data.

Refresh checklist

The sequence used to update and verify recurring data.

Refresh status

Information showing when and how data was last updated.

Regression output

A table of fitted-model statistics and coefficients.

Reject table

Rows excluded from the clean dataset with documented reasons.

Relationship

A key-based connection between model tables.

Relative reference

A reference that adjusts when copied.

Replace

A controlled substitution of matching content.

Return array

The aligned range containing the result.

Ribbon

The tabbed command area at the top of Excel.

Row integrity

Keeping all values belonging to a record together.

Rows area

Fields displayed vertically as categories.

Rule precedence

The order in which overlapping rules are evaluated.

SORT

Sorts an array by a specified position.

SORTBY

Sorts an array using one or more corresponding arrays.

STDEV.S

Sample standard deviation.

SUBSTITUTE

Replaces specified text occurrences.

SUBTOTAL

A function that can calculate while ignoring filtered-out rows.

SUM

Adds numeric arguments or range values.

SUMIF

Sums values meeting one criterion.

SUMIFS

Sums values meeting multiple criteria.

Scenario

A named set of input values.

Sensitivity analysis

Examining how outputs change when assumptions change.

Serial date

Excel’s numeric representation of a date or time.

Sheet protection

Restrictions on editing specified worksheet elements.

Show Values As

A secondary calculation applied to aggregated PivotTable values.

Skewness

A measure of distribution asymmetry.

Slicer

A button-based visual filter for tables or PivotTables.

Slope

Expected change in y for one-unit change in x in a fitted line.

Sort key

The field used to determine order.

Sort level

One criterion in a multi-level sort.

Source sheet

A sheet that preserves imported or manually entered input data.

Spill

Automatic placement of array results in neighboring cells.

Spill range

The cells occupied by a dynamic-array result.

Spill reference

A reference such as A2# to an entire spilled result.

Status bar

The bottom area that can show quick calculations and workbook state.

Structured reference

A formula reference using table and column names.

TEXTBEFORE

Returns text before a delimiter.

TEXTJOIN

Joins text using a delimiter and optional blank handling.

TEXTSPLIT

Splits text into an array using delimiters.

TODAY

Returns the current system date.

TRIM

Removes extra standard spaces while leaving single spaces between words.

Time fraction

The fraction of a day representing time.

Timeline

A date-specific visual filter for PivotTables.

Total row

An optional summary row using functions such as SUBTOTAL.

Transformation

A change applied to query data.

Two-way lookup

A lookup using both row and column criteria.

UNIQUE

Returns distinct values or rows.

Unmatched key

A source key with no corresponding master record.

Unpivot

Converting multiple measure columns into attribute and value rows.

Used range

The worksheet area Excel considers used.

VALUE

Converts recognizable text into a number.

Validation rule

The condition that determines allowed values.

Values area

Fields aggregated as sums, counts, averages, or other measures.

Version history

A recoverable record of saved file versions in supported storage.

Visual hierarchy

The ordering that guides attention through a report.

Volatile function

A function recalculated whenever Excel recalculates, even if direct inputs did not change.

Wildcard

A pattern character such as * or ? used in text criteria.

Workbook

A file that can contain worksheets, formulas, tables, queries, models, and charts.

Workbook protection

Restrictions on workbook structure such as adding or deleting sheets.

Worksheet

One grid inside a workbook.
